hook_text: Same 24 blocks. Wrapping needed: 98 or 52? Shape decides.
clip_script: Take twenty-four one-centimetre cubes. Every prism you build from all of them has a volume of twenty-four cubic centimetres. But the surface areas differ. A long row: ninety-eight square centimetres. A flat slab: sixty-eight. A chunkier block, four by three by two: fifty-two square centimetres. The more compact the shape, the smaller the surface area.
visual_style: 24 blocks snake into a long row with 98 glowing faces, reshape into a slab with 68, then a chunky block with 52; a wrapping-paper meter drops.
pacing: Three reshapes with counters, then the takeaway.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to see what happens when a cube doubles.
